concepts.bodyMd:
Gadwal was the **oldest Samsthan**, situated between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers. It was separated from Raichur district and later joined Mahbubnagar district, ruling for nearly **600 years** before merging into Andhra Pradesh state in **1956**.

**Geography and Resources**

*   Situated 1,063 feet above sea level.
*   Lakes, wells, and ponds were the main water sources.
*   Had 360 villages, bordered by Alampur Taluk (east), Tungabhadra river (south), Raichur district (west), and Krishna river (north).

**Administration**

*   Annual income was 10 lakh rupees; annual expenditure was Rs. 7,31,308.
*   Rulers had authority over civil and criminal judgements and could appoint their own administrative staff.
*   Maintained infantry, cavalry, and artillery forces.
*   Historic and spiritual villages under the Samsthan included Pudur, Vallur, Rajavolu, Aija, Maldakal, Chagadona, Beechupalli, and Sri Rama Avadhuta Agraharam.

**Dynasty and Origins** The rulers belonged to the **Mustipalli dynasty** and were Pakanati Reddis who followed the Veera Vaishnava tradition and built many temples. Construction of the Gadwal fort began in the 17th century and continued into the early 18th century. Pudur was the first capital, with Chenna Keshava Swamy as the presiding deity — it appears in gazettes as Keshavapuram. Pudur gained prominence during the Chalukya period; Chalukya-Pallava wars fought here were won using the _Gadha_ (mace) and _Walu_, giving the town its earlier name Gadavala, which later became Gadwal.

**Founder — Polani Reddy alias Buddha Reddy** He was a great warrior and expert in war strategy and politics, appointed as ruler of Manalibeludoni, Raichur, Alampuram Adavani, Aija, and Mosalakallu by the Kakatiya ruler Pratapa Rudra. Between 1686–87, his descendants extended the kingdom by winning Nandyala, Siriguppa, Ahobilam, Siddapuram, Bandi Atmakur, and Sirivella, and defeated the Kandenavolu Nawab, seizing his flag and emblem. They held the titles **Nadagowda** and **Sir Nadagowda** until 1600 AD.

**Succession**

| Ruler | Period | Key Contribution |
|---|---|---|
| Raja Shobhanadri | up to 1712 | Founder of Gadwal Samsthan; built a well and fort in Aija; built Ramalingeswara Temple in Kasi (1712) |
| Kalla Venkanna | to 1719 | Successor ruler |
| Ramanaiah (caretaker) | 1719–1724 | Appointed by Shobhanadri's queens |
| Ammakkamma (1st wife of Shobhanadri) | 1724–1725 | Ruler |
| Lingamma (2nd wife of Shobhanadri) | 1725–1738 | Developed the Samsthan; built the Beechupalli fort's foundation, Sangala and Tandrapati ponds, and Lingamma well; adopted Tirumala Raya |
| Raja Tirumala Rao | 1738–1742 | Completed the Beechupalli fort |
| Mangamma (1st wife) | 1742 (brief) | Ruler |
| Rani Chokkamma (2nd wife) | 1742–1747 | Built the Anjaneya Swamy temple in the Nizam's fort at Beechupalli |
| Raja Rama Rao (adopted, brother-in-law) | 1746–1762 | Merged Boravelli villages with Gadwal; defeated Rajaprolu Zamindars, captured 8 villages; defeated the Kurnool Nawab and seized his Dhakka and Flag; built the Chenna Keshava Swamy Temple at Bethendla |
| Raja Chinna Somabhupal | 1762–1793 | Title _Bhupalu_; defeated Upperu and Gangapalle rulers, merged Dharur Paragana with Gadwal; built the Keshavalaya shikaram, Ramalayam (1779), and Bhudevi temple (1788) |
| Raja Chinna Ramabhupal | 1793–1806 | Resolved a border dispute with Raichur's Hanumantha Desai and Narasinga Rao with Nizam's help |
| Bhupala (son-in-law) | after 1806 | Became ruler |
| Rani Venkata Lakshmamma (3rd wife of Sitaram Bhupal) | 1844–1865 | Built Keshavalaya Gopuram, Mahadwaram (1849); adopted Ramana (son of Venkatapuram Gomam Krishna Reddy) with Nizam's permission, naming him Raja Ram Bhupal |
| Maharani Adi Lakshmi Devamma | last ruler | Her elder daughter married the Domakonda King; Gadwal merged with Hyderabad State on **17 September 1948** |

**Literature** Gadwal Samsthan actively patronized poets and writers. **Pedda Soma Bhoopal** began the tradition of felicitating poets and singers in the month of Magha. Notable court poets and their works included:

*   **Kanadam Peddana Somayaji** — wrote the Balakanda of the Ramayana under the title _Bhadra Parinayam_.
*   **Keeriti Venkatacharyulu** — wrote Sanskrit works _Alankara Koustubham_, _Bhava Shatakam_, _Jhunja Marutam_, _Shringaralahari_, _Hayagreeva Dandakam_, and the masterpiece _Achalatmaja Parinayam_.
*   **Kama Samudram Appalacharyulu** (titled _Vidvatkavikunjara_) — wrote _Krishna Leela Tarangini_ and the Kishkinda Kanda of the Ramayana.
*   **Karnamadakala Ananthacharyulu** — wrote _Acharya Vimshati_, _Andhra Shabda Chintamani_, _Madana Vijaya Banam_.
*   **Kottapalli Ramachandra Charyulu** (titled _Vidvanmaha Kavi_) — wrote verse and interpretations of the Ayodhya Kanda.
*   **Gargyapuram Subba Shastri** (titled _Ubhaya Kavita Nissahaya Sahiti Dhureena_) — wrote verse and interpretations of the Aranyakanda.
*   **Hosadurgam Vedanthacharyulu** (Administrative Officer) — wrote _Acharya Vaibhavam_, _Sri Krishna Brahma Tantrarya Vedapadastavam_.
*   **Pullagummi Venkata Charyulu** (master of Raja Seetarama Bhoopala Rao) — wrote _Alamkaravali_, _Adilakshmi Karnapurnam_, _Andhra Vyakarana Sutravali_.
*   **Pullagummi Ahobila Charyulu** (an eminent astrologer) — wrote _Abhinavatidhi Valli_, _Druksiddha Grahaganitam_, _Surya Siddantasaaram_.
*   **Chetluri Narayana Charyulu** (Scientific Officer) — wrote _Pratapa Rudreeyasaram_.
*   **Puranam Deekshacharyulu** — wrote _Ramachampuvu_, _Ramanrupakarnapurnam_, _Kavyotkarsha_, _Keshava Suprabhatam_.
*   **Puranam Narasimha Charyulu** — engaged in a scholarly argument with Tirupati Venkata Kavulu; wrote _Janaki Parinayam_, _Sri Rama Bhupa Charitra_.
*   **Gadepalli Veeraraghava Sastri** — wrote _Sri Satyavaralakshmi Dhruva Charitram_, _Sri Rani Satyavaralakshmi Ramayanam_, _Tripurantaka Sthala Mahatyam_.
*   **Adipudi Prabhakara Kavi** — wrote _Poundarikam_, dedicated to Gadwal Chenna Keshavaswamy.
*   **Pokuri Kashipathi** (court poet of Rani Adilakshmamma) — wrote _Sarangadhareeya Nirdhostya Nirvachanam_, _Shuddandhra Harishchandropakyanadyanakendra_.
*   **Peddamandadi Venkata Krishna Kavi** — wrote _Nirvachana Bhakti Vijayam_, _Maruti Vilasam_, _Gadwal Samsthan Charitram_, _Reddykula Nirnayachandrika_, _Keshava Vilasam_.
*   **Sri Rama Narasimha Murthy Kavulu** (twin poets, in Prince Krishna Bhoopala's court) — wrote _Nirupamana Deeksha_, _Sri Madhandra Bhagavatam_.
*   **Sri Dharmavaram Krishnamacharyulu** — awarded the title _Andhra Nataka Pitamaha_ by the Gadwal rulers; wrote many books.

Wanaparthy Samsthan covered a total area of **450 sq. miles** with **124 villages**. Its first capital was Nuguru, and the Samsthan was initially known as Nuguru Samsthan; the first ruler, Ramakrishna Rao, later shifted the capital to Wanaparthy, after which the Samsthan took that name.

**Dynasty** The rulers carried the surname **Janumpally** and belonged to the Motati Reddy caste and Penubala Gotram, residing initially at Kurnool. The founder was **Veera Krishna Bhoopati Reddy alias Veera Krishna Reddy**.

**Succession**

| Ruler | Key Details |
|---|---|
| Veerakrishna Reddy | Native of Janumpally (Nandyala Taluk, Kurnool); ruled parts of Nandyala as a satrap of the Vijayanagara kings; later occupied villages around Panagallu Fort in Mahaboob Nagar and ruled Nuguru as capital |
| Vemudi Venkata Reddy | Fourth generation from Veera Krishna Reddy; praised by Golconda Nawab Abdullah Qutub Shah in 1633 after occupying Nellore and Udayagiri forts for the Nawab with a 10,000-strong army; received additional villages as reward |
| Gopala Rayalu | Son of Venkata Reddy; held the title _Bahiri_ |
| Venkata Reddy (adopted) | Had no male heir; Gopala Rayalu adopted him. He fell into debt, failed to pay impost to the Nizam Nawab, was defeated by the Nizam's army, and died by suicide out of humiliation. He was given the title _Sawai_ by the Delhi Sultan; built the village Gopalpet in honour of his foster father Gopala Rao and named his own son Gopal Rao; appointed his brother Ranga Reddy as ruler of the newly built Gopalapet with 12 adjoining villages |
| Ramakrishna Rao-I | Popular ruler; jailed for three years by the Nizam due to a conspiracy by his cousins, later released on discovery of the truth; received the title _Raja Bahadur_ from the Nizam in 1817; shifted the capital from Nuguru to Wanaparthy |
| Raja Rameshwara Rao (adopted) | Provided welfare facilities to his people; maintained cordial Nizam relations and assisted in battles; presented with a Sword, Pistol, and Rifle by the Nizam Government in 1861; introduced a permanent tax system on the British model |
| Raja Ramakrishna Rayalu (adopted) | Died suddenly |
| Rameshwara Rao-II (adopted) | Efficient administrator; the Samsthan reached its peak under him — implemented welfare schemes, dug wells and ponds for agriculture, and strengthened law and order |

Raja Rameshwara Rao had two sons: the elder, **Sri Krishnadeva Raya**, married Sarala Devi (daughter of Munagala ruler Raja Venkata Ranga Rao); the second, **Sri Ramadeva Raya**, married Kumudini Devi (daughter of Pingali Venkata Ramareddy). Sarala Sagar, a large pond, was constructed in Sarala Devi's name. After Krishna Devaraya's death, disputes arose between Rani Sarala Devi and Raja Ramadeva Raya, which relatives and close friends resolved. Sarala Devi's son, **Raja Rameshwara Rao**, was an educationist and, after the Samsthan's merger, became a **Member of Parliament**.

**Literature**

*   **Raja Bahari Gopalarayalu** (titled _Asta Basha Kavi_, described by historians as _Asta Basha Gopala Raya_) — wrote _Ramachandrodayam_, _Sringara Manjari Banam_.
*   **Veera Raghavacharyulu** (court poet) — wrote a 1770 commentary on the Sanskrit Bhagavatam titled _Veera Raghaveeya Vyakya_.
*   **Akshintala Subba Sastri** (resident of Recherla village, 19th century) — wrote _Bhashyardha Ratnamala_; a great stoic in theology.
*   **Singampalli Narasimha Siddhanti** (astrologer) — wrote _Bhoobramana Bhranthi Nirasana_.
*   **Archakam Ayyamacharyulu** (Peddamandadi village) — wrote _Peddamandadi Chennakesava Satakam_ and _Rameshwara Vijayam_.
*   **Hosadurgam Krishnamacharyulu** (judicial officer) — wrote _Rameshwara Vijaya Champavu_ (a Prabhantham on the Samsthan's ruler), along with _Alankara Maniharam_, _Unnmatta Pandavam_, _Keshavostava Malika_, _Prasannananda Lahari_, _Raghunatha Vijayam_, _Sri Krishna Pancha Ratnamala_, _Srinivasa Vilasam_, _Sri Ramayana Vaibhavam_.
*   **Sannidhanam Suryanarayan Sastri** — dedicated his _Khanda Kavyam Puvvula Thota_ to Wanaparthy ruler Late Sri Krishnadevaraya; Krishna Devaraya's wife Sarala Devi assisted in its publication.

Atmakuru Samsthan, in Mahaboob Nagar district, was earlier known as **Amarachinta Samsthan**, covering an area of 190 sq. miles under the Amarachinta and Vaddemanu (Vardhamanu) paraganas. Tivudampalli was the first capital, before the rulers later shifted to Atmakur.

**Dynasty** The rulers belonged to the **Pakanati Reddy dynasty** and carried the surname **Mukkera**. The founder was **Gopala Reddy**.

**Succession**

| Ruler | Key Details |
|---|---|
| Gopala Reddy | From Chandragiri (near Tirupati, Chittoor district); served Gona Buddha Reddy at Tirupati, who in 1292 made him ruler of Vardhamanapuram |
| Chinna Gopi Reddy | Son of Gopal Reddy; became ruler of Atmakur Samsthan; in 1363 obtained the Sarnadha Gowda Watan region of Panchamahal Taluk as _sanad_ from Katabhupala; assisted the Bahamani Sultans and received the posts of Nadegowda, Sarnadha Gowda, Deshmukh, Deshpandya, and Desaigiri in Ferozegad (Muzaffar Nagar Paragana) |
| Chandra Reddy | Son of Chinna Gopi Reddy; a great devotee, built the Kurumurthi Temple |
| Gopi Reddy-II | Grandson of Chandra Reddy; contemporary of Golconda Sultan Abdullah Qutub Shah; fought on behalf of the Golconda rulers, defeated Gopala Rao who had occupied Gurramkonda fort, and jailed him; received the Allipuram Jagir and permission to maintain 500 munsabdari and 200 sawaris; obtained Amarachinta and Vardhamanapuram. His brother **Saheb Reddy** was appointed ruler of Kadechur and Magatha regions by the Nizams |
| Sarva Reddy | Became ruler after Gopi Reddy |
| Sarva Reddy-II (grandson) | Assisted Aurangzeb's army, received the Duppalli Jagir, Flag, Nagara, 500 sawaris, and royal emblems |
| Timma Reddy-I (son) | Received cooperation from the Peshwa rulers of Maharashtra, who gave him Amarachinta and Vaddemanu Paragana on annual contract of 50,000; Raja ChandraSena built Chandragad and Dharmapuram villages in his wife's name and made Timma Reddy Deshmukh of those villages |
| Saheb Reddy (great-grandson of Timma Reddy) | In 1748, during the establishment of the Asaf Jahi Kingdom, helped Asaf Jahi rulers in the Carnatic wars and received the title _Sawai_ |
| Pedda Venkata Reddy (7th generation from Saheb Reddy-II) | Contemporary of Asaf Jahi ruler Sikander Jha; close to the Sultan; obtained Amarachinta and Vaddemanu Paraganas with the help of Deewan Chandulal; shifted the capital from Tivudampalli to Atmakur town |
| Balakrishna Reddy | Son of Pedda Venkata Reddy; became ruler |
| Soma Bhoopal Rao | Son of Balakrishna Reddy; received Amarachinta and Vaddemanu Paraganas as permanent Bilmukhth on payment of Rs. 52,201 (raised to 70,000 during the period of Prime Minister Salarjung) |
| Raja Sitarama Bhoopal Rao | Son of Soma Bhoopal; maintained friendly relations with the Nizam rulers |
| Sawai Raja Sri Rama Bhoopal Balwant | Son of Sitarama Bhoopal; developed Atmakur |
| Bhagyalakshmamma | Wife of Sri Rama Bhoopal Balwant; last ruler; after her, the Samsthan was merged into Hyderabad state |

**Literature**

*   **Surapuram Keshavaiah** (c. 1760) — prominent poet; wrote _Niroshtya Ramayanam_, dedicated to Atmakur ruler Sri Raja Somabhoopal.
*   **Tirumala Bukkapatnam Rangacharyulu** — wrote _Gunaratnakara_, _Padmini Parinaya Champuvu_, _Geervana Kriti_.
*   **Tirumala Bukkapatnam Srinivasa Charyulu** (titled _Tarka Teertha_, _Balasaraswati_) — wrote _Jambhavati Parinayam_, _Tatva Marthanda Prabha Mandalam_, _Durmada Nirmadhanam_, _Nanjaraju Champavu_, _Rajasekhara Charitra_, _Surapura Venkataguru Charitra_.
*   **Deekshitula Narasimha Sastri** (given the title _Mahakavi_ by Amarachinta rulers) — wrote _Lakshmana Parinayam_, _Nidurashwatta Mahatyam_, _Sri Ranga Mahostava Varnamalika_, _Satyanarayana Vratakalpam_.
*   **Harithi Deeksha Charyulu** — wrote _Alankara Manimala_, _Acharya Vimshati_, _Mahantharlapamala_.
*   **Poet Arishanapalamu Venkatadwari** — wrote _Laxmi Sahasra Vyakhyanam_. Other poets included Tirumala Venkatacharyulu, Tirumala Bukkapatnam Butchi Venkatacharyulu, and Mudigonda Nagalinga Sastri.
*   **Deekshitula Papa Sastry** — wrote _Chenchu Natika_, _Hanumath Charitra_.
*   The rulers patronized **Tirupati Venkatakavulu**, who dedicated their book _Srinivasa Vilasam_ to Sitarama Bhoopal; poet **Karyamapudi Rajamannaru** wrote _Sri Sitarama Bhoopala Vilasam_ at the rulers' request.

Part of Mahboob Nagar district, Jataprolu Samsthan had **9 villages** across **191 sq. miles**, with an annual income of **2 lakh rupees**. Its rulers served as satraps of the Vijayanagar kings, Golconda Sultans, and Asaf Jahis. After the capital shifted from Jataprolu to Kollapur, the Samsthan came to be known as **Kollapur Samsthan**.

**Dynasty** The rulers were **Padmanayakas**, from the royal families that ruled Devarakonda and Rachakonda, carrying the surname **Surabhi** and belonging to the Recharla gotra. The dynasty's founder was **Chevvi Reddy**, popularly known as **Bethala Nayaka**.

**Succession**

| Ruler | Key Details |
|---|---|
| Sarvangyasinga Bhoopala Surabhi | Founder of the Padmanayaka Dynasty |
| Mahipati | Belonged to this dynasty |
| Surabhi Madhava Rayulu (5th generation) | A great scholar; wrote _Chandrika Parinayam_; received the Jataprolu Samsthan as a gift from the Vijayanagara kings |
| — | His sons received the Jataprolu Samsthan as a _sanad_ from Golconda King Abdulla Qutub Shah in AD 1650 |
| Surabhi Laxmana Raya | Shifted the capital from Jataprolu to Kollapur in 1840; rulers thereafter were called Kollapur Kings |
| Laxmi Jagannadha Rao (son of Raja Laxmana Rao) | Ruled 1851–1854; received the titles Raja Bahadur and Nizam Nawaz Wanth from the Nizam |
| Venkata Jagannadha Rao | Last ruler; during his regime, Kollapur Samsthan merged with Hyderabad State |

**Literature**

*   **Madhava Rayulu** and his son **Narsing Rao** were both great poets — Madhava Rayulu wrote _Kshatrakhelanam_, and Narsing Rao wrote _Shudrasmriti_.
*   **Chintapalli Gopala Mantri** (17th century) — felicitated by the Samsthan rulers for his Sanskrit work _Arya Satakam_.
*   **Veera Raghava Kavi** — wrote _Madhura Vani Vilasam_.
*   **Akshintala Subba Sastri** (1807–1871) — wrote an explanation to the _Brahma Sutrabhasyam_ titled _Dhashyardha Ratnamala_.
*   **Akshintala Singara Sastri** — wrote _Annapurnastakam_, _Dwadasha Manjari_, _Bhaskara Khandam_, _Srisaila Mallikarjuna Ratnapanchakam_.
*   **Yunayavalli Krishnamacharyulu** — wrote _Astaprasarama Satakam_ (Sanskrit), _Niroshtya Krishna Satakam_, _Jataka Chandrika Vyakya_, _Rasagyanandam_, _Sri Krishna Champuvu_.
*   **Vellala Sadashiva Sastri** (1861–1926) — on the orders of ruler Surabhi Laxmaraya, wrote a noted commentary on Madhava Rayulu's _Chandrika Parinayam_; other works include _Kavyalankara Sangraha Vimarshanam_, _Andhra Dasharupaka Vimarshanam_, _Veerabhadriya Khandanam_, _Velugoti Vamsha Charitra_, _Surabhi Vamsha Charitra_, _Kanteerava Charitra_, _Ramachandra Charitra_, _Namireddy Charitra_, _Yatininda Nirakanaram_, _Ramanuja Gopala Vijayam_.
*   **Sridhara Krishna Sastri** — wrote _Sri Rama Mandahasam_.
*   **Hosadurgam Krishnamacharyulu** — wrote _Laxmi Vilasa Champuvu_, _Madanagopala Mahatyam_.

Papannapeta was the **oldest Samsthan in the Nizam State**, established during the reign of Delhi Sultan Feroze Shah Tughlaq. The entire Methuku region was part of the Samsthan and it continued in that form until 1707; its size subsequently reduced under Mughal rule, the Deccan Subedars, and later under the Asaf Jahi regime.

**Succession**

| Ruler | Key Details |
|---|---|
| Rani Shankaramma | Belonged to the 12th generation of the Samsthan's rulers, from which its recorded history is available; mistress of Raja Venkata Narasimha Reddy; took charge after her husband's demise. An able administrator and warrior, she raised a large army and repeatedly defeated the Maratha Army that forcibly collected Chauth and Sardeshmukhi taxes from the public, earning accolades from the Nizam kings, who presented her the title **Raibagan** ("lioness") and a royal emblem — the title gradually changed to Saibagan and Raibegum. She dug ponds and irrigation canals for agricultural development, and, having no male heir, adopted Sadashiva Reddy of Domakonda Samsthan |
| Sadashiva Reddy | Popular ruler and great warrior; his mistress **Parvathi** (daughter of the Gadwal ruler) was herself an expert in warfare and fought alongside him as bodyguard, saving his life several times. In 1795, when the elder son of Asaf Jahi ruler Nizam Ali Khan revolted with the help of Galib Jung and Sadashiva Reddy, the Nizam's army — initially defeated by Sadashiva Reddy — returned with French forces' assistance, defeated him, and took him captive; he and Parvati were imprisoned and killed there. His brother ruled the Potlacheruvu Samsthan, and his son **Narasimha Reddy** succeeded him. Rulers of this Samsthan held the title **Char Hazar** |
| Raja Venakta Durga Reddy | Ruled in the early 20th century; after his sudden demise, the Samsthan came under the control of the Court of Wards until 1927 |
| Rani Venkata Laxmamma Sardesai (widow) | Took charge after the Court of Wards period |
| Raja Ramachandra Reddy | Became the final ruler; **Papannapet Samsthan merged into Hyderabad State in 1948** |

The Samsthan's rulers built forts at Sangareddy, Velamakanne, and Ramayampet.

**Literature**

*   **Rani Venkata Laxmamma Sardesai** — a great poetess; wrote _Manasa Bodha_.
*   **Feelkhana Shankara Rayakavi** (court poet) — wrote _Sugnana by Deepa Guru Geethas_.
*   **Chidere Laxmana Sastri** — wrote _Medak Samsthandheeswara Charitra_.

Domakonda Samsthan was part of Nizamabad district, initially called **Bikkavolu Samsthan** (Bikkavolu is today's Biknur). Its rulers served as satraps to the Golconda Nawabs and Asaf Jahi rulers. **Rajanna Chowdhary** shifted the capital from Bikkavolu to Kamareddypeta, and his son **Rajeshwara Rao** later shifted it from Kamareddypeta to Domakonda, after which the Samsthan took its name.

**Dynasty** The rulers were **Pakanati Reddis**, close relatives of the Gadwal and Atmakur rulers. Belonging to the Kaminedu dynasty, they were called **Kamineni**, with Rachulla as their gotra and Bikkavolu Siddarameshwara as their presiding deity. The Nizams, impressed by the Kaminedu's services, gave them responsibility of Bikkavolu (in the Metuku region); Kamineni was renamed **Kamireddy**, giving rise to Kamareddi town.

**Succession**

| Ruler | Key Details |
|---|---|
| Kacha Reddy-I | Ruled Rayadurgam |
| Reddy Bhoopati alias Bhogi Reddy (son) | Mistress: Rani Dechambika; had three sons — Kacharreddy-II, Malla Reddy, Bomma Reddy |
| Kacharreddy-II | Wife Machamamba; son Yella Reddy |
| Kacharreddy-III (son of Yellareddy-Mallamamba) | Had four sons: Jangama Reddy, Kama Reddy, Yella Reddy-II, Malla Reddy |
| Kama Reddy | In AD 1636, obtained the Domakonda Samsthan as _sanad_ from the Golconda rulers |
| Malla Reddy | Great devotee; given many titles by the Golconda Sultan; many villages (Yella Reddy, Macha Reddy, Kamareddy, Jangampalli) are named after this line of rulers and exist today |
| China Kamireddy (son of Yella Reddy) | Held the title Deshmukh |
| Pota Reddy (grandson) | Held the title Desai |
| Rajanna Chowdhary (son) | A strong ruler who shifted the capital from Bikkavolu to Kamareddy; survived an army sent by the Nizam after enemies complained against him, and thereafter maintained cordial relations with the Nizam, who was impressed by his war skills |
| Rajeshwara Rao-I (son) | Shifted the capital from Kamareddy to Domakonda; helped the Nizam in a war against the Chennur rulers, and was appointed ruler of Bikkavolu and Chennur; the Samsthan grew significantly under his regime |
| Pedda Rajeshwar (son) | Close friend of the Nizam's Prime Minister Chandulal; had no children and appointed his brother Anna Reddy as ruler |
| Anna Reddy | Ruler of Domakonda Samsthan |
| Raja Ramachandra Rao (son of Raja Umapati) | Ruled Domakonda during 1927; married the daughter of the Gadwal ruler |
| Raja Someshwara Rao | Last ruler; his son Krishna Ram Bhoopal went to Gadwal on adoption; during his rule, **Domakonda Samsthan merged with Hyderabad State** |

**Literature**

*   **Pattametta Somanatha Somayaji** (Kamareddy's court poet) — wrote _Sootasamhita_, _Brahmottara Khandam_, _Vishista Andhrokti_.
*   **Lakshmipathi** — wrote _Sri Krishna Vilasam_, _Acharya Vijayam_, _Sri Madhupakyonam_, _Neela Vivaham_.
*   **Adipudi Prabhakara Kavi** — wrote _Umapatabhyudayam_ on the instructions of the Domakonda ruler, comprising 286 prose and poetry sections, in which the Kamineni dynasty's history was recorded.
*   **Seshadri Ramana Kavulu** and Domakonda court poet **Pedda Mandadi Venkata Krishna Kavi** — jointly wrote _Reddy Kula Nirnaya Chandrika_.

Munagala Samsthan, also called Munagala Zamindari or Munagala Paragana, is one of the **oldest Samsthans**, located in Nandigama Taluk of Krishna district. In 1959, after the formation of Andhra Pradesh, it was made part of Nalgonda district for administrative convenience, covering an area of around **100 sq. miles**.

During the last Kakatiya rulers, Rudrama Devi and Pratapa Rudra, the Samsthan's army chiefs — **Mukundappa, Surappa, and Narasanna** — were highly popular; no further history of the Samsthan is recorded until the 18th century. In 1790, during the battle between the French and the East India Company, ruler **Keesara Lachhamma Rao** provided military assistance to the British, who felicitated her for it. In the early 20th century, the Samsthan's income was one lakh twenty thousand rupees, and its rulers bore the title **Jabdatulakran**.

**Succession**

| Ruler | Key Details |
|---|---|
| Gurlapati Ayanna Desai | Ruled 1652–1693; his son died during this period |
| Daughter-in-law (of Keesara family) | Unable to handle affairs, handed responsibility to her brother Mukundappa |
| Keesara Mukundappa | A great warrior; assisted Mughal King Aurangazeb in Deccan battles and got Munagala as _Sanad_ |
| Narasanna (son) | Ruled briefly after his father's death |
| Lacchayamma (wife of Narasanna) | Great politician and efficient administrator; the Samsthan saw great development under her regime |
| Venkata Ramanna (son of Lacchayamma) | — |

Raja Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao was a great patron of the Telugu language. Although Munagala Samsthan was part of British India, Ranga Rao's literary and cultural activities were carried out in the Nizam State — he helped establish the **Sri Krishna Devaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam**, reconstructed the Maha Linga Temple in the Samsthan's village Tadwai, and brought the inscribed rock pillars of the Cheruku Reddy dynasty to Nadigudem fort for preservation. He had two sons, Ramakrishna Reddy (elder) and Gopala Krishna Reddy (younger), and a daughter, **Sarala Devi**, who married Wanaparthy ruler Raja Krishnadeva Raya. In **1947, Munagala Samsthan was merged into Madras State**; Raja Venkata Ranga Rao died in 1958.

**Literature**

*   **Varada Raja Nandikeshwara Kavi** — wrote _Shivatatva Sudhanidhi_, _Sethu Mahatyam_, _Rameshwara Kshetra Mahatyam_.
*   **Komarraju Ramalinga Kavi** — wrote _Veerabhadra Satakam_, _Srigiri Malleswara Satakam_, _Veerabhadra Karunya Nidhi_.
*   **Komarraju Venkata Shivudu** — wrote _Repala Rajalinga Satakam_ (127 seesa poems).
*   **Komaraju Venkata Lakshmana Rao** (Diwan of Munagala Samsthan) — established the _Vignana Chandrika Grantha Mandali_ and edited _Andhra Vignana Sarvaswam_ as a researcher.

Paloncha, in present-day Khammam district, was popularly known as **Shankaragiri Samsthan**. Before the separation of Khammam district from Warangal, it extended across 6 Taluks with an area of **800 sq. miles**; being a forest area, its population and income were limited. Its rulers were satraps of the Nizam kings.

Rekapalli and Bhadrachalam were originally part of this Samsthan. Bhadrachalam was initially with the Nizam State, later passed to British possession in 1860, joining the Central Province, and in 1874 became part of Madras State. During the initial period, the Samsthan received 5,000 Peshkas from the Nizam (raised to 18,000 in 1935); its income was 6 lakh rupees and it paid forty thousand rupees as annual impost.

**Origins** During the regime of Golconda king Mohammed Quli Qutub Shah, his army chief **Ashwarao**, son of Kalamalayam of the Padmanayaka dynasty, was highly popular. Paloncha rulers descend from Ashwarao. Paloncha, Bhadrachalam, and Ashwaraopet were the capitals of his descendants; they lost control of the Samsthan for a time, during which it was ruled by the Kandimalla, Tandra, Jalagam, Damera, and Mutyala families. The Rekapalli Samsthan (8,000 peshkas) passed to the Mareddy dynasty, belonging to Vararamachandrapuram.

**Succession**

The Paloncha rulers, descendants of the Padmanayaka dynasty, served as army chiefs and cavalry heads under the Kakatiya ruler Pratapa Rudra.

*   **Appanna** — ruler of Shankaragiri and Husnabad during 1324; his descendants continued as satraps of the Musunuri, Padmanayaka, Bahamani, and Golconda Sultans until 1698.
*   The 18th-generation ruler received **Badshahi Munsabdari** from Aurangazeb.
*   **Zaffer-ud-Doulah**, Army Chief of the Moghuls, murdered Paloncha ruler **Narasimha Ashwa Rao** in 1769 and robbed the treasury; after this, Paloncha became a Samantha (feudatory) Kingdom of the Asaf Jahis. **Raja Narasimha Ashwa Rao and Ramachandra Ashwarao** ruled the Samsthan for some time thereafter.
*   In **1796**, **Venkata Rama Narsimha Apparao** received the titles Raja Bahadur and Sawai Munsabdar, along with a Flag, Nagara, and Nobuth, and permission to maintain a cavalry of 2,000 and infantry of 3,000.
*   **Narasimha Ashwarao** succeeded him as ruler. Settipalli Zamindars filed a court case to claim the Paloncha Samsthan, dragging on until 1858 and financially weakening the Samsthan as a result.
*   **Sri Sita Rama Chandra Sawai Ashwa Rao**, with the help of Hyderabad Diwan Salarjung-I, won this case and became ruler; however, during his regime the Samsthan fell further into debt, and the British took possession of the Bhadrachalam and Rekapalli regions. Unable to bear the debt burden, he died.
*   **Lakshmi Narasayamma** (his mother) took over the Samsthan. Due to non-payment of Rs. 6,00,000, a court order allowed the lender to collect taxes for 12 years and take possession of the Samsthan; the Nizam paid Rs. 3,00,000 to the lender and, for the remaining balance, handed over the villages of Malluru and Ramanuja Varam. Rani Lakshmi Narasayamma died in 1875.
*   **Parthasarathi Apparao** (her adopted son) ruled Paloncha efficiently and received many titles from the Nizam.
*   **Vijaya Apparao** was the last ruler; the Samsthan merged with Hyderabad State after the **Police Action**.

**Literature**

*   **Srinathuni Venkata Rama Kavi** — the Samsthan's first poet; wrote _Sri Rama Pattabishekam_ (also called _Ashwaraya Charitra_).
*   **Raja Parthasarathi Apparao** (titled _Sahitya Visharada_) — a great literary patron.
*   **Sri Kottapalli Venkatarama Lakshmi Narayana Sharma** (his court poet) — honoured Krishnamurthy Sastri with 1,000 rupees and a stoned ring for translating the Aadi and Sabha Parvas of the Mahabharata; also wrote _Paloncha Samsthan Charitra_.
*   **Sri Raja Vijaya Apparao** patronized the _Andhra Vangmaya Samithi_, established at Burgampadu and Paloncha.

Boravelli was a popular Samsthan of Telangana. Its rulers were **Pakanati Reddys**, belonging to the Middimalla Gothram, carrying the surname **Mushtipalli**, with **Polukanti Someshwara** as their presiding deity. This Samsthan merged with **Gadwal** after a few years.

**Succession**

| Ruler | Key Details |
|---|---|
| Nadagoudu Tamma Reddy | First ruler; ruled the Aija region with Boravelli as capital; wife Machamma |
| Nalla Reddy (son) | Two wives — Mallamba and Timmamba |
| — | Children of Mallamba: Pedda Soma and Chinna Soma. Children of Timmamba: Tammareddy, Papareddy, and Mallamba |
| Pedda Soma | Married Lacchamamba; son Venkata Reddy, who wrote the composition _Raghavabyudayam_ and ruled the Samsthan for a few years |
| Raja Thirumala Rao | Ruled the Samsthan 1738–1742 |
| Chokkamma (wife) | Ruled 1742–1747 after Thirumala Rao's death |
| Rama Rao (adopted, brother-in-law of Chokkamma) | Came to Boravelli on adoption; Chokkamma called him to Gadwal and asked him to take over the kingdom and protect her sons. He adopted Raja Chinna Soma Bhupal and Raja Chinna Rama Bhupal, sons of Rani Chokamma, and **merged Boravelli Samsthan into Gadwal Samsthan** |

**Literature**

*   **Garudachala Kavi** — wrote _Kausaleya Charitram_.
*   **Veera Raghava Kavi** — wrote _Madhura Vani Vilasam_.
*   **Sanjeeva Kavi** — wrote _Chandragadopakyanam_.

* * *

The Samsthanas that began under Kakatiya rule continued through the Qutub Shahi and Asaf Jahi periods before finally merging into India. Their rulers introduced numerous welfare programmes, constructed lakes for agricultural development, and built temples. They were also the first to introduce printing machines in Telangana, and the newspapers this enabled brought public awareness and drew people towards the independence movement. As patrons of literature who encouraged scholars and poets, they contributed significantly to the development of the Telugu and Sanskrit languages and to Telangana's culture more broadly — some of their constructions were destroyed over time, while others were developed into educational institutions or remain as tourist spots today.
